To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Ordovician biodiversification in Argentina, and probably in the whole Gondwana, was a mosaic of different patterns of faunal assemblage development that reflect the complex interaction between the geodynamic and palæogeographic setting of each basin, and the latitudinal location of the basins within Gondwana.

the structure and diversity of the early Ordovician (late Arenig) faunal associations in the west of Argentina were controlled by the interplay of two large-scale factors: (1) the geodynamic setting and (2) the latitude of the basins.
the early Ordovician radiation in western Argentina is characterized by a mosaic of type assemblages that are controlled by environmental dynamics coupled with the latitudes of the different basins.

the early Ordovician biodiversification and its possible causes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ordovician biodiversification was the result of the combined action of several large-scale and regional factors, and that the Ordovican radiation is not the result of a single process.

the early Ordovician radiation of the Palaeo- and Bathyurid faunas was not a uniform phenomenon but rather a complex mosaic of different responses to environmental dynamics at the scale of the palaeobiogeographic provinces.
the Ordovician evolutionary faunas and radiation are a global phenomenon but with a wide range of local expressions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Ordovician biodiversification in western Argentina was mainly controlled by the interplay between the palaeogeographic and geodynamic settings of the basins and the latitudinal distribution of the faunas.

the early Ordovician (early Arenig) faunal diversity and assemblages from west Argentina are largely controlled by the interplay of the regional palaeoenvironmental conditions with the latitudinally controlled palaeogeographic and tectonic setting.
the early Ordovician radiation of marine invertebrates is not a simple phenomenon that occurred at the same time and with the same magnitude everywhere.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, at the regional scale, the Ordovician evolutionary faunas are not monolithic, but rather are characterised by a number of different assemblages, each one reflecting a distinct combination of the regional environmental and palaeogeographical settings.

the Ordovician evolutionary faunas were the result of the complex interplay among the different geodynamic and climatic conditions of each region and the intrinsic biological properties of each group of organisms.
, although the early Ordovician radiation is a well-known phenomenon, it has not been studied in detail in terms of its expression in different geodynamic settings and latitudes.
